## First, stop it safely
• Unplug it or flip its circuit breaker off (electric dryers usually use a double breaker).
• For a gas dryer, unplugging is enough. You don't need to shut off the gas unless you smell gas. If you do, leave and call the gas company.
• If it's been running a long time, let it cool before you touch anything inside.

## Common causes (roughly most to least likely)

1. Dirty moisture sensor (if you use "auto dry" or "sensor dry")
The dryer thinks clothes are still wet and keeps going.
• Look inside the drum near the lint filter for two metal strips.
• Wipe them with rubbing alcohol or a vinegar-soaked cloth. Dryer sheet residue builds up there.
• Try a timed dry cycle. If that stops normally, the sensor is likely the issue.

2. Clogged lint filter or vent
Poor airflow means clothes take forever to dry, so sensor cycles keep running.
• Clean the lint screen.
• Check that the outside vent flap blows air strongly while running.

3. Faulty timer (older dryers with a mechanical dial)
If the dial isn't advancing during a timed cycle, the timer motor has likely failed. It's a fairly common, replaceable part.

4. Stuck start button or switch
If the dryer starts as soon as power is restored, without pressing start, the start switch or a relay may be stuck.

5. Control board relay stuck (digital models)
If the display shows the cycle ended but the drum still spins, a relay on the board may be welded shut. This usually means replacing the board.

6. Faulty cycling thermostat
It can keep the heat on or interfere with how the cycle ends.

## Helpful details if you want more specific help
• Brand and model
• Gas or electric
• Dial or digital controls
• Does it happen on timed dry, sensor dry, or both?
• Is the heat still on, or just the drum spinning?
• Does the timer or display count down?

Until it's fixed, don't leave it running unattended. Overheating is a fire risk.
its a Beko condenser dryer, digital. the drum turns a bit every few minutes after it says End. clothes are dry though

That's normal. It's the anti-crease feature, not a fault.

After the cycle finishes, Beko dryers tumble the drum briefly every few minutes so dry clothes don't sit in a heap and wrinkle. It runs with no heat and continues for a set time after "End" (often up to about 2 hours, depending on the model) or until you open the door.

To stop it:
• Open the door, or
• Press the On/Off button

To turn it off for future loads:
Many Beko models have an option button labeled Anti-crease, Wrinkle Care, or a shirt/hanger icon. If it's lit or selected, deselect it before starting. Some models have it built in and can't disable it. Your manual (or the model number, usually inside the door) will confirm which yours is.

While you're at it, since it's a condenser dryer, empty the water tank and clean the condenser unit and lint filters regularly to keep drying times short.
